seoTitle: Change DNS on Namecheap: Add TXT, CNAME & MX Records
metaDescription: Learn how to access Namecheap's DNS management panel and add or edit TXT, CNAME, and MX records for email, domain verification, and hosting.
intro: Managing DNS records in Namecheap lets you connect email services, verify domain ownership, and configure third-party hosting, but it means understanding how records like TXT, CNAME, and MX each work. This guide covers accessing the DNS panel and adding these records correctly.

steps.heading: Access the DNS management panel
steps.body: Log in to Namecheap and open the Advanced DNS section for the domain you want to update.

steps.heading: Add or edit a TXT record
steps.body: TXT records are commonly used for domain verification, so add one with the exact value provided by the service requesting it.

steps.heading: Add or edit a CNAME record
steps.body: CNAME records point a subdomain to another domain name, useful for connecting services like email platforms or third-party tools.

steps.heading: Add or edit an MX record
steps.body: MX records route email for your domain, so set the priority and mail server values exactly as your email provider specifies.

steps.heading: Confirm records are set up correctly
steps.body: Double-check each record for typos and allow propagation time before troubleshooting further if a service isn't verifying.

faq.question: What is a TXT record typically used for?
faq.answer: TXT records are most often used to verify domain ownership for services like email providers or third-party platforms.

faq.question: Why would I need to add an MX record?
faq.answer: MX records tell the internet where to deliver email for your domain, so they're essential if you're setting up custom email service.

faq.question: How can I speed up DNS propagation?
faq.answer: You can't force it directly, but lowering the TTL value ahead of time can help changes take effect faster.

faq.question: What happens if I enter a DNS record incorrectly?
faq.answer: An incorrect record can prevent verification or email delivery from working, so it's worth double-checking values against what the service provided.
